missionPremise: Items 18, 20, 21 (floodplain acreage + FIRM panel citation, USDA SSURGO soil, electric/gas provider) are resolvers, not composition wiring: per the dispatch, 'the acquisition and the honest-absence semantics are the actual work, and they do not need to wait' for R-01's composition root, which is why this lane could close cleanly without R-01 landing first. Gas is scoped out of any acquisition attempt by standing operator ruling (2026-09-03_gas_utility_service_rail_closed_unacquirable.md) -- the only correct work item there was a properly-cited structural absence, not a lookup.
completionPredicate: For each of the three families, a resolver exists in packages/engine-core/src/<family>/ returning a present/absent discriminated union, unit-tested against both outcomes, merged to hauska-engine main behind a green CI check-run, and independently run against live upstream data for both real Bastrop parcels named in the dispatch (48021:52726, 48021:52727) producing a correct, cited, non-fabricated result -- not a fixture replay for the live-verification claim specifically. All three met; see per-family evidence below. Not included in this predicate, and explicitly out of scope per the dispatch: wiring any of the three into a PDF section (R-01's composition root does not exist yet) and any change to packages/adapters or engine-core/src/site-plan.
scopeBasis: Dispatch names packages/adapters/ as CTX-B's for the sprint (Round Rock reconciliation, Kyle provenance, corpus-divergence rewrite in packages/adapters/src/local/setbacks/) and engine-core/src/site-plan/ as R-01's (composition re-cut). Both were read (to learn the present/absent convention and the existing SSURGO/FEMA adapters) but never written -- verified at every commit by `git status`/PR diff showing zero paths under either directory. Three new sibling directories were created under packages/engine-core/src/ matching the existing fact-family convention (flood-hazard-fact/, well-fact/, special-district-fact/, rrc-pipeline-fact/, utility-easement/) rather than extending any of those.

item_18_floodplain_acreage_firm_panel.evidence: packages/engine-core/src/floodplain-acreage-fact/. Live 2026-09-07 for both real Bastrop parcels: present, sfhaAcres=0 (two non-SFHA Zone X hits, one of them the 0.2%-annual-chance shaded-X zone -- a real measured zero, not a whole-parcel flag or a fabricated absence), firmPanel present (FIRM_PAN 48021C0355F, effective 2023-05-09, from NFHL layer 3 -- a citation nothing in this codebase read before this lane, since layer 28's own DFIRM_ID is only a 6-char county id). 5 unit tests, including a byte-for-byte replay of the real captured response.

item_20_soil_ssurgo.evidence: packages/engine-core/src/soil-fact/. Live 2026-09-07 for both parcels: present, 'Bosque loam, 0 to 1 percent slopes, occasionally flooded', well drained, hydrologic group B, mukey 393277 -- independently corroborates the floodplain family's 0.2%-annual-chance finding above from an unrelated federal source. 4 unit tests including a degraded-but-present case (one of the two USDA upstreams down, the other still answers, matching the adapter's own resilience contract).

item_21_electric_gas.evidence: packages/engine-core/src/electric-provider-fact/. Electric: live 2026-09-07 for both parcels returns 3 overlapping HIFLD candidates (a real HIFLD territory-overlap data-quality artifact, disclosed as ambiguous:true rather than silently narrowed) -- present, cited. Gas: resolveGasProviderFact() always returns the same structural, cited absence per the 2026-09-03 ruling -- correct behavior, not a placeholder. 7 unit tests total across both.

what_remains_open: R-01's composition root does not exist yet, so none of these three resolvers is wired into an actual generated PDF section. Per the dispatch this is expected and explicitly not this lane's job ('wiring a resolver into a section is trivial once R-01 exists') -- but it means the dispatch's literal check ('present and cited on a live-generated PDF for a real parcel') is satisfied at the resolver level, not yet at the PDF level. Whoever builds the composition root should treat these three modules' exported resolve*Fact functions as the substrate.

This lane has no Postgres credential (CORTEX_DATABASE_URL/TXGIO_DATABASE_URL/DATABASE_URL/SUBSTRATE_DATABASE_URL all unset in this environment). All three resolvers query live public upstreams directly rather than the Factory's already-staged tables (tx_fema_nfhl_flood_zone for flood zones; tx_utility_territory_staging for HIFLD electric, confirmed real and tracked in legacy-design-tools per doc-repo-26). Once a credential exists, item 18 could be revisited to prefer the already-staged flood-zone table (cheaper, no live FEMA call per report) and item 21's electric resolver could read the staged table directly instead of re-querying HIFLD live -- open questions for whoever holds that credential, including whether the 139 rows staged 2026-08-14 are still current.

Item 21's electric result is an honest disclosed ambiguity (3 HIFLD candidates) for the two Bastrop test parcels, not a single resolved name. A future pass could add a tie-break heuristic (e.g. TYPE=MUNICIPAL preferred inside city limits) but that is a product/UX decision about how to present ambiguity, not a data gap, and was deliberately left undecided here rather than guessed.

Smart Site MCP access in this session was gated above this session's tier for get_smart_site -- real parcel geometry came from Bastrop County's own public ArcGIS parcel layer instead. Not a defect, just worth knowing for the next lane that expects MCP-sourced geometry to just work.
